newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-DUBIOUS PENALTY HELPS LANUS TO 2-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUBIOUS PENALTY HELPS LANUS TO 2-0 WIN.

text.p: A dubious penalty set Lanus of Argentina on their way to a 2-0 win at home to Colombia's Santa Fe in the first leg of the South American Conmebol Cup final on Wednesday.
The Colombians were more than holding their own until Lanus striker Ariel Lopez went tumbling over in the Santa Fe penalty area in the 30th minute.
Lopez did not appear to be fouled but the referee awarded a penalty which was converted by Oscar Mena.

Lanus, an unfashionable club from a Buenos Aires suburb who have grown in stature in the last three years and are currently second in the Argentina championship, extended their lead when Ariel Ybazaga scored with a header in the 78th minute.
Santa Fe have the advantage of playing at 2,600 metres altitude when they are at home in the second leg on December 4.
The Conmebol Cup was inaugurated in 1992 as a local version of Europe's Uefa Cup. It has been won three times by Brazilian clubs and once by an Argentine side.
